title: Stored DOM-XSS via [chat] BBCode `quote` username in chat rich-editor extension (plugins/chat)
summary: The chat plugin's ProseMirror (WYSIWYG / rich editor) extension `toDOM` callback concatenates `node.attrs.username` directly into an `innerHTML` template literal. `username` is taken verbatim from the first `;`-separated segment of the `quote="..."` attribute on a user-authored `[chat]` BBCode block, with no escaping anywhere on the markdown -> token -> ProseMirror node -> DOM path. Any low-privileged user can post markdown that, when later opened in the rich editor by another user (most importantly an admin/moderator clicking 'Edit'), executes attacker JavaScript in the victim's authenticated origin context. The site default `default_composition_mode = 1` (rich) puts every new account into the vulnerable editor.

source.actor: any user able to author markdown (TL0/TL1+)

flow.note: BBCode parser accepts `"[^"]+"` (and smart-quote variants) inside `quote="..."`; the raw value lands in tagInfo.attrs.quote with `<`, `>`, `=`, etc. intact.
`const [username, messageIdStart, messageTimeStart] = tagInfo.attrs.quote.split(';')` -> attacker controls `username` (first segment).

username is stored as token attr `data-username` (raw) and as the content of an `html_inline` token (also raw). markdown-it's HTML renderer escapes attrs at render time, but the rich-editor parser bypasses HTML rendering.
ProseMirror parse hook reads `token.attrGet('data-username')`, which returns the raw unescaped string, and stores it as `node.attrs.username` on the `chat` schema node.

When the editor mounts/edits, `convertFromValue` runs `this.parser.convert(this.schema, value)` over the post's raw markdown, then commits the resulting doc to the view, which calls each node's toDOM.
SINK: `userElement.innerHTML = `${node.attrs.username}${formattedDateTime}``. Browser parses the resulting markup; an `` payload inside the username fires immediately.

reachability.trigger: Any user opens the attacker's post in the rich editor (default composition mode). Practical triggers: (a) admin/mod clicks Edit on the attacker's post; (b) any user uses Quote-whole-post to insert the post's markdown into their own composer; (c) attacker reopens their own draft (self-XSS, useful for chains).
preconditions: chat plugin enabled (default on chat-bundled sites)
victim's composition_mode == 'rich' (site default since rich editor became default)

impact.execution_context: victim browser, on Discourse origin, with session cookies and CSRF token available
primitives: exfiltrate session cookies (httpOnly limits direct cookie reads, but JS-on-origin can call any API the session is authorised for)
call admin REST API with X-CSRF-Token meta tag content (full admin takeover if victim is staff)
install malicious theme/component -> persistent JS for every visitor -> full forum takeover
trigger email-takeover flows when victim is a normal user

disclosure.notes: Not yet checked against Discourse security advisories. Recent commits (Mar-May 2026) fix several near-by issues (assignee XSS, category description XSS, omniauth provider escape, review-queue highlightWatchedWords XSS, codes_to_img). None of those touch plugins/chat/assets/javascripts/lib/rich-editor-extension.js. Confirm against Discourse GHSA list before reporting.

remediation.minimum_fix: Escape `node.attrs.username` before interpolation, e.g. `${escapeExpression(node.attrs.username)}` (discourse/lib/utilities), or build the username span via createElement + textContent.
remediation.preferred_fix: Stop using innerHTML in toDOM altogether for user-controlled attrs - construct DOM nodes via createElement and assign user values via textContent / set attributes via setAttribute. Apply the same audit to: serializeNode's bbCodeAttrs string-builder (line 144, separate quoting bug, no DOM impact).
remediation.regression_test: Add an integration test analogous to plugins/chat/test/javascripts/components/rich-editor-extension-test.gjs asserting that an ``-bearing username produces a chat-transcript-username span with no `` descendant.
